name: Udokan
citation: Russian State Reserves figures as published by Udokan Copper (about 2.7 Bt at 1.0 % Cu, 26.7 Mt Cu)
notes: USGS sedCu lists Udokan without tonnage; one of the largest undeveloped copper deposits

name: Jinding
citation: Xue et al. 2007, Ore Geology Reviews (220 Mt at 6.08 % Zn, 1.29 % Pb)
notes: largest sandstone-hosted Zn-Pb deposit; not in the USGS MVT/SEDEX compilation

name: Olkusz-Zawiercie (Upper Silesia-Krakow district)
citation: order of magnitude from district production since the 12th century plus remaining resources (Polish Geological Institute district summaries)
notes: silver-lead mining at Olkusz documented from the 13th century; Triassic Muschelkalk ore-bearing dolomite

name: Bytom (Upper Silesia)
citation: order of magnitude from district production since the 12th century plus remaining resources (Polish Geological Institute district summaries)
notes: Bytom silver-lead mining is recorded in 1136; exhausted in the 20th century

name: Tri-State district (Picher-Joplin)
citation: order of magnitude from the district's 1850-1970 production (about 7 Mt Zn and 2 Mt Pb in concentrates) as summarised by the USGS
notes: Mississippian cherty limestone runs; not in the USGS MVT/SEDEX compilation

name: Old Lead Belt (Southeast Missouri)
citation: order of magnitude from about 8-9 Mt Pb produced 1869-1972 (USGS summaries of the Southeast Missouri lead district)
notes: Bonneterre Dolomite; the Viburnum Trend deposits are separate entries from the USGS compilation

name: Upper Mississippi Valley district
citation: order of magnitude from district production (about 1.3 Mt Zn and 0.45 Mt Pb) as summarised by the USGS (Heyl et al. 1959)

name: North Pennine orefield (Alston Moor and Weardale)
citation: order of magnitude from about 4 Mt lead concentrate produced (Dunham 1990, Geology of the North Pennine Orefield)
notes: silver-lead mines of Alston worked for the English crown from the 1130s

name: Derbyshire Peak District orefield
citation: order of magnitude from district lead production since Roman times (Ford and Rieuwerts, Lead Mining in the Peak District)
notes: Roman lead pigs from Derbyshire date from about AD 80

name: Mendip Hills (Charterhouse)
citation: order of magnitude; Roman lead and silver extraction at Charterhouse from AD 49 (dated lead pig)
notes: small district; calamine (smithsonite) worked in the 16th-19th centuries

name: Cartagena-La Union
citation: order of magnitude from Punic-Roman silver and 19th-20th century Pb-Zn production (Manteca and Ovejero 1992)
notes: silver mines of Carthago Nova worked from the 3rd century BC

name: Linares-La Carolina
citation: order of magnitude from Roman and 19th-20th century lead production (district once the world's leading lead producer)
notes: Castulo silver-lead mines worked from Iberian and Roman times

name: Resolution
citation: Rio Tinto Annual Report 2023 via Resolution Copper project overview (1,787 Mt at 1.54 % Cu, 0.035 % Mo; 4,500-7,000 ft below surface)
notes: Buried under the Whitetail Conglomerate and Apache Leap Tuff; the USGS global copper assessment lists it as a prospect without tonnage and carries its older estimate as Superior East (996 Mt at 0.50 % Cu), which this row replaces

name: Rammelsberg
citation: Large and Walcher 1999, Mineralium Deposita 34 (27 Mt at 14 % Zn, 6 % Pb, 2 % Cu, 140 g/t Ag, 1 g/t Au)
